clue.text: Skill that's not at all pronounced

indicators.note: pronounced tells us the word meaning 'not at all' is to be taken by its sound alone

parts.note: nohow is a dialect word for not at all, in no way

explanation.surface: Someone's talent is so modest it barely shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR gave 'ref' for 'not'. 'pronounced' looks like 'marked' in the surface but signals that NOHOW, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical expertise in getting something done is a skill.

clue.text: King with a sort of shirt slipped into a cooler garment

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: slipped into means put inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a fan cools you down
a T-shirt is a sort of shirt, giving the letter T

explanation.surface: A monarch wearing a shirt has changed into a more comfortable robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose tunic or dress is a type of clothing.

clue.text: Reports after head is dismissed as too old

indicators.note: head is dismissed means the first letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: coverage is the reporting of news

explanation.surface: Reports say the head was sacked for being past it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link word: the result comes after the beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beyond a permitted age limit means being older than allowed.

clue.text: Hard current measure covering rent in this part of England

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means the first pieces sit above the next

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
amps measure electric current
to hire is to rent

explanation.surface: Tough measures on rents are being applied in a region of England.
explanation.walkthrough: HAMPSHIRE is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a county on the south coast of England, so a region of the country.

clue.text: Direction to government leader I dropped in political centre

parts.note: west is a compass direction

indicators.note: dropped means taken out, so the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a minister heads a government department

explanation.surface: Instructions to a party leader dropped in at the seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR lost the 'I' in the clue. Dropping I from MINISTER leaves MINSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The district holding the Houses of Parliament is the heart of British politics.

clue.text: Help steal piece of luggage

parts.note: to give someone a hand is to help them
to bag something is to take it, often without permission

explanation.surface: A thief's accomplice helps to make off with someone's bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bag carried by hand is a piece of personal luggage.

clue.text: Either female or male name

explanation.surface: A name that works for a woman or a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either' is a link; each sense is a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a female bird, and the same word is a familiar short form of the man's name Henry.

clue.text: Record score

definitions.meaning: a cut or score made in something

explanation.surface: A sports report notes a record score.
explanation.definitionFit: To notch up a win is to record it, and a notch is also a nick or score cut into wood.

clue.text: Boastful threats from assassin holding a duke

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a bravo is a hired killer or thug

explanation.surface: A hitman takes a nobleman hostage and makes threats.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a swaggering show of boldness and boasting.

clue.text: Animals' keeper has to move articles over road

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the earlier pieces sit above the next

parts.note: to go is to move
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A zookeeper must shift objects across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tends goats is a keeper of animals.

clue.text: No slave's accepted thus as member of society

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a freeman is a free person, not a slave; the 's is not a letter here
so means in this way, thus

explanation.surface: A former slave is admitted to the community as a full member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted' also nods to the Free and Accepted Masons.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasonry is a fraternal society, and its members go by this name.

clue.text: Ornate headgear I found in ancient Irish site

indicators.note: found in means placed within, so the letter goes inside the place name

parts.note: Tara is the hill in County Meath where the ancient High Kings of Ireland sat

explanation.surface: A jewelled crown turns up during an excavation in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled crown or coronet is a decorative piece of headwear.

clue.text: Name of first lady's partner — son, too

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis, was partnered with Adam
s is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A President's wife and their son share the surname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' looks like a President's wife, but it is Eve; John Adams's wife Abigail was a first lady too, so the surface works both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common surname, borne by two US presidents.

clue.text: Hygienic measure opening to coastal inlet required

parts.note: a mouth is an opening, as of a cave or river
the Wash is a broad inlet on the east coast of England

explanation.surface: Sanitary precautions are needed at the entrance to a bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rinsing with an antiseptic liquid is a step taken for oral hygiene.

clue.text: Composed a foreign story about northerner

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story
a Lapp is a person from Lapland in the far north

explanation.surface: Someone wrote a foreign tale about a person from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' reads as 'wrote' but is the adjective meaning calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being calm and unruffled in a crisis is to be collected.

clue.text: Military force of king, say, gets order from Napoleon

parts.note: a legion is a large body of soldiers
taken as written
in card games the king is one of the honours, the top cards

explanation.surface: A king's army receives a command from Napoleon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' reads as a command, but it is an order of merit; Napoleon founded this French decoration in 1802.
explanation.definitionFit: This is France's highest order of merit, instituted by Napoleon Bonaparte.

clue.text: Reforming mood in one part of Russian church

indicators.note: reforming means forming again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mood of reform takes hold in part of the Russian Church.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulbous cupolas top many Russian Orthodox churches.

clue.text: Traveller's approach relatively honest, we hear

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, so the definition reads as a traveller is

parts.note: a way is an approach or method

indicators.note: we hear tells us the next word is to be taken by its sound alone

parts.note: fairer is more fair, or relatively honest

explanation.surface: A traveller's methods are reported to be fairly honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone journeying on foot.

clue.text: Wrongfully intern American shellback

indicators.note: wrongfully suggests the letters are handled wrongly and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A US citizen is unjustly detained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongfully' rearranges INTERN AMERICAN; the answer is Coleridge's poem's sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellback is slang for an old, seasoned sailor, which is what Coleridge's narrator is.

clue.text: Examination control at university

parts.note: to check is to control or restrain
being up means in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Exams are controlled at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical or general inspection is a type of test.

clue.text: Like part of UK side in America

definitions.meaning: belonging to England, one of the UK's four nations
in US pool and billiards, this word means sidespin put on the ball

explanation.surface: A national team playing in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names things from England; in American billiards the same word means spin put on the ball from striking it off-centre.

clue.text: Hot new scarf put on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on top means the scarf sits above the next piece

parts.note: a stole is a long scarf worn over the shoulders

explanation.surface: A fashionable new scarf is worn on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' is not heat or fashion but slang for stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for goods recently taken by theft.

clue.text: Deal with error in scientific expedition

parts.note: to field a question or problem is to deal with it
a trip is a stumble or mistake

explanation.surface: Researchers must handle a blunder made on their outing.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing to study something in its natural setting is a scientific expedition.

clue.text: Old fogeys serve parties

parts.note: to do is to serve, as in that will do
dos are parties or celebrations

explanation.surface: Elderly bores attend parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodos are people hopelessly behind the times, like the extinct bird.

clue.text: Close junction when it gets dark

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a T-junction is where one road meets another at right angles, giving the letter T

explanation.surface: A road junction is closed at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' reads as a verb but is the adjective meaning near.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness are the period after the sun goes down.

clue.text: Inclined to scrape front of doormat

parts.note: to rake is to scrape or drag with a toothed tool

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone is minded to scrub the mat by the door clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' is not a mood but a slope, as a theatre's raked stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A raked stage or seating area slopes, so it is tilted or sloping.

clue.text: Most roast lamb I cooked is heavenly tasting

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new arrangement
most of a word means all but its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone reckons their roast lamb tastes divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' takes the last letter T off ROAST, leaving ROAS; 'cooked' rearranges ROAS, LAMB and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the gods, so this adjective means divinely delicious.

clue.text: A pair of hands, in a certain respect

parts.note: W and E, the West and East hands, are a partnership at bridge

explanation.surface: Someone lends a hand in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge the four players, or hands, are named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential wonder, a respect mixed with fear.

clue.text: Immediate reply in letter I posted

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Someone sent back a quick answer by post.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp retort, like a fencer's swift return thrust.

clue.text: Novel type of theatre we are backing

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: Noh is a classical form of Japanese theatre
were is we are with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A theatre company supports a new kind of drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is the noun, Samuel Butler's 1872 satire.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Butler's satirical book of 1872 is a well-known novel.
